title: Global Career Development and Internal Mobility Policy
text:
# Global Career Development and Internal Mobility Policy
**Region:** Global (all offices)
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2025
**Document ID:** HR-POL-GLOBAL-043

## Purpose and Eligibility
The Company supports employees in building skills, exploring career paths, and applying for internal roles. Regular employees may participate in development programs from their first day, subject to role requirements, business priorities, and local law.

## Individual Development Plans
Employees and managers should review an Individual Development Plan at least twice each year. The plan may include skill goals, mentoring, project assignments, certifications, job shadowing, and formal learning. Development goals do not change the employee's current job level or guarantee promotion.

## Learning Budget
Eligible full-time employees may receive up to $1,500 per calendar year for approved external courses, certifications, or conferences. Part-time eligibility is prorated by scheduled hours. Requests must be submitted through the Learning Portal before registration and must include the business purpose, provider, cost, and expected completion date.

The manager and People Operations must approve the request before the employee incurs an expense. Reimbursement requires proof of payment and completion within 30 days after the learning activity.

## Mentoring and Career Conversations
Employees may request a mentor through the internal mentoring program. Managers should hold a career conversation at least twice per year and discuss skills needed for possible next roles. Managers must not retaliate against employees who explore internal opportunities.

## Internal Job Applications
Employees may apply for posted internal roles after completing six months in their current role, unless HR approves an exception for restructuring, relocation, or business-critical circumstances. Employees must meet the qualifications listed in the posting. Current managers are informed after the candidate enters the interview stage, unless local law or HR guidance requires another process.

Selection decisions are based on qualifications, documented performance, business needs, and fair hiring practices. Applying for an internal role does not guarantee an interview, transfer, or promotion.

## Contact
Learning and Development Team - learning@company.com
Internal Mobility Team - mobility@company.com

title: US Compensation and Rewards Policy
text:
# US Compensation and Rewards Policy
**Region:** United States
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2025
**Document ID:** HR-POL-US-040

## Scope
This policy applies to regular full-time and part-time US employees. It covers base pay, annual merit reviews, incentive eligibility, promotions, and compensation changes. Collective bargaining agreements and local law control where they provide more favorable terms.

## Pay Philosophy
The Company sets pay using market data, internal role levels, skills, sustained performance, and geographic labor-market considerations. Compensation decisions must be consistent, explainable, and free from discrimination or retaliation.

## Salary Bands
Each job level has a published minimum, midpoint, and maximum salary range. The employee's range and current compa-ratio are available through the HR portal. Hiring managers may not promise compensation outside the approved range without Compensation Team approval.

## Annual Merit Review
Annual merit reviews are normally effective April 1. Employees must be active and in good standing on the review date. Merit increases are based on performance, position in the salary range, market movement, and available budget. A merit review does not guarantee an increase.

Managers must submit written recommendations to HR by February 15. Employees returning from approved protected leave must be evaluated on the same performance period and may not be penalized because of the leave.

## Promotions and Market Adjustments
A promotion requires a documented increase in job scope and approval from the manager, department leader, and Compensation Team. Promotion increases normally take effect at the start of the next payroll period after approval. Market adjustments may be made when reliable market data shows a material gap; they are separate from performance increases.

## Bonuses and Incentives
Eligible employees may participate in an annual incentive plan. Target percentages are determined by job level and plan document. Actual payment depends on Company results, individual performance, and active-employment requirements in the applicable plan. Incentive payments are discretionary unless a written plan states otherwise.

## Payroll and Pay Questions
Employees should report a suspected payroll error through the HR portal within 30 days of the pay date. Payroll investigates and corrects confirmed errors in the next practicable payroll cycle. Employees should not send bank details or tax documents through ordinary email.

## Contact
Compensation Team - compensation@company.com
Payroll Support - payroll@company.com

title: Global Workplace Conduct and Anti-Harassment Policy
text:
# Global Workplace Conduct and Anti-Harassment Policy
**Region:** Global (all offices)
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2025
**Document ID:** HR-POL-GLOBAL-042

## Standards of Conduct
Employees must act lawfully, honestly, respectfully, and in the Company's legitimate interests. The standards apply at Company locations, during business travel, at work events, in digital collaboration spaces, and when representing the Company online.

Prohibited conduct includes harassment, discrimination, bullying, retaliation, threats, violence, conflicts of interest that are not disclosed, misuse of confidential information, falsification of records, and intentional misuse of Company systems or assets.

## Reporting Concerns
Employees may report a concern to their manager, Human Resources, Legal, the Ethics Hotline, or any other manager they trust. Reports may be made verbally or in writing. Employees do not need to report to the person involved in the concern.

Ethics Hotline: ethics@company.com
Confidential reporting portal: ethics.company.com/report

## Investigation Process
The Company will acknowledge reports when possible, assess immediate safety or legal risks, and assign an impartial investigator. Participants must preserve relevant records and cooperate honestly. Investigations are conducted as confidentially as practical, but confidentiality cannot be guaranteed.

The investigator documents relevant evidence and provides findings to HR and Legal. Corrective action may include coaching, training, written warning, reassignment, loss of access, or termination, depending on the facts and applicable law.

## Non-Retaliation
Retaliation against a person who raises a concern in good faith, participates in an investigation, requests an accommodation, or exercises a legal right is prohibited. Suspected retaliation should be reported promptly through any channel listed above.

## Employee Responsibilities
Employees must complete assigned conduct and anti-harassment training, protect investigation confidentiality, and report urgent safety concerns immediately to local emergency services or Security.

title: US Health Insurance Benefits Summary
text:
# US Health Insurance Benefits Summary
**Region:** United States
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2024
**Document ID:** HR-POL-US-021

## Plan Options
- PPO Gold Plan: $150/month employee premium, $500 individual deductible.
- PPO Silver Plan: $90/month employee premium, $1,500 individual deductible.
- HDHP + HSA Plan: $40/month employee premium, $3,200 individual deductible,
  Company contributes $1,000/year to employee HSA.

## Eligibility
Full-time employees (30+ hours/week) are eligible from day 1 of employment.
Part-time employees are not eligible for Company-subsidized health plans.

## Dependent Coverage
Spouses, domestic partners, and dependent children up to age 26 may be
added during open enrollment or within 30 days of a qualifying life event
(marriage, birth, adoption, loss of other coverage).

## Open Enrollment
Held annually in November for coverage effective January 1. Changes outside
open enrollment require a qualifying life event and must be reported to
HR within 30 days of the event.

## Contact
Benefits Team - hr-benefits@company.com | 1-800-555-0142

title: EU Parental Leave Policy
text:
# EU Parental Leave Policy
**Region:** European Union (Germany, France, Netherlands offices)
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2022
**Document ID:** HR-POL-EU-014

## Overview
This policy applies to all full-time employees based in EU member-state
offices, in addition to statutory parental leave entitlements provided by
local law, whichever is more generous to the employee.

## Eligibility
All full-time employees are eligible from their first day of employment,
consistent with EU Directive 2019/1158 on work-life balance for parents.

## Leave Entitlement
- Birthing parent: 16 weeks fully paid leave, plus any additional statutory
  maternity leave required by local law.
- Non-birthing parent / secondary caregiver: 10 weeks fully paid leave.
- Leave may be taken within 12 months of the qualifying event, or as
  otherwise permitted by local statutory law.

## Pay During Leave
100% of base salary, coordinated with statutory maternity/parental pay
schemes to avoid double payment.

## How to Apply
Submit local country HR leave form (see country-specific intranet page)
at least 60 days before the anticipated start date, in accordance with
local statutory notice requirements.

## Contact
EU HR Benefits Team - hr-benefits-eu@company.com

title: US Parental Leave Policy
text:
# US Parental Leave Policy
**Region:** United States
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2021
**Document ID:** HR-POL-US-014 (v1.0)
**Status:** Archived - superseded by HR-POL-US-014 (v2.0), effective March 1, 2023

## Overview
This policy applies to all full-time employees based in the United States.

## Eligibility
Employees must have completed at least 90 days of continuous employment prior
to the expected date of birth, adoption, or foster placement.

## Leave Entitlement
- Birthing parent: 8 weeks of fully paid leave.
- Non-birthing parent / secondary caregiver: 4 weeks of fully paid leave.
- Leave must be taken within 6 months of the qualifying event.

## Pay During Leave
100% of base salary is paid during the leave period through the Company's
short-term disability and parental leave benefit program. Leave does not
count against the employee's standard PTO balance.

## How to Apply
Submit Form HR-014 to your manager and to hr-leaves@company.com at least
30 days before the anticipated start date (or as soon as practicable for
unplanned events such as premature birth).

## Contact
HR Benefits Team - hr-benefits@company.com

title: US Parental Leave Policy - 2023 Amendment
text:
# US Parental Leave Policy - 2023 Amendment
**Region:** United States
**Effective Date:** March 1, 2023
**Document ID:** HR-POL-US-014 (v2.0) - SUPERSEDES v1.0

## Summary of Changes
Effective March 1, 2023, the Company has expanded parental leave benefits
for all US-based full-time employees. This amendment supersedes and replaces
the parental leave terms described in HR-POL-US-014 (v1.0, dated Jan 1, 2021)
in their entirety.

## Eligibility
Employees must have completed at least 60 days of continuous employment
(reduced from 90 days) prior to the qualifying event.

## Leave Entitlement
- Birthing parent: 12 weeks of fully paid leave (increased from 8 weeks).
- Non-birthing parent / secondary caregiver: 8 weeks of fully paid leave
  (increased from 4 weeks).
- Leave must be taken within 12 months of the qualifying event (increased
  from 6 months).

## Pay During Leave
100% of base salary, unchanged from prior policy. Leave does not count
against standard PTO balance.

## How to Apply
Same process as before: submit Form HR-014 to your manager and to
hr-leaves@company.com at least 30 days before the anticipated start date.

## Contact
HR Benefits Team - hr-benefits@company.com

title: Global Performance Management Policy
text:
# Global Performance Management Policy
**Region:** Global (all offices)
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2025
**Document ID:** HR-POL-GLOBAL-041

## Purpose and Scope
This policy establishes a consistent performance-management process for regular employees worldwide. Local law, works council requirements, and collective bargaining agreements apply where they impose additional requirements.

## Goal Setting
Managers and employees must agree on role goals within 30 days of the start of each performance year or within 30 days of a transfer or promotion. Goals should identify measurable outcomes, role expectations, development priorities, and any dependencies outside the employee's control.

## Check-ins
Managers must hold a documented one-to-one check-in at least once each quarter. Check-ins should cover progress, priorities, support needed, feedback, wellbeing, and changes to goals. Employees may request an additional check-in at any time.

## Annual Review
The annual review cycle closes on December 31. Managers provide a written assessment using the Company's performance factors: results, collaboration, customer impact, judgment, and role-specific capability. Employees may submit written comments within 10 business days of receiving the review.

A performance rating must be supported by documented examples from the review period. Protected characteristics, approved leave, disability accommodations, complaints made in good faith, and legally protected activity must not influence a rating.

## Performance Improvement Plan
A Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) may be used when performance is materially below role expectations after coaching and feedback. A PIP normally lasts 60 to 90 days and must state the performance gaps, measurable expectations, support offered, check-in dates, and possible outcomes. HR must review a PIP before it is issued.

## Calibration and Appeals
People leaders and HR may calibrate ratings to promote consistency across teams. Employees who believe a review contains a factual error or prohibited bias should first discuss it with the manager and may contact HR within 30 calendar days.

## Contacts
People Manager Support - peoplemanagers@company.com
People Operations - peopleops@company.com

title: US Paid Time Off (PTO) Policy
text:
# US Paid Time Off (PTO) Policy
**Region:** United States
**Effective Date:** January 1, 2024
**Document ID:** HR-POL-US-007

## Overview
Applies to all full-time, non-union US employees.

## Accrual
- Years 0-2 of service: 15 PTO days/year, accrued at 1.25 days/month.
- Years 3-5 of service: 20 PTO days/year, accrued at 1.67 days/month.
- Years 6+ of service: 25 PTO days/year, accrued at 2.08 days/month.

## Carryover
Up to 5 unused PTO days may be carried over into the next calendar year.
Any balance above 5 days is forfeited on December 31, unless local state
law requires otherwise (e.g., California does not permit "use-it-or-lose-it"
policies; unused PTO carries over in full for CA-based employees).

## Requesting PTO
Submit requests through the WorkdayHR portal at least 5 business days in
advance for planned absences. Manager approval is required.

## Payout on Termination
Unused, accrued PTO is paid out at the employee's final base rate upon
termination, in accordance with state law.

## Contact
HR Benefits Team - hr-benefits@company.com

title: Global Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
text:
# Global Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
**Region:** Global (all offices)
**Effective Date:** June 1, 2023
**Document ID:** HR-POL-GLOBAL-030

## Work Arrangements
- **Hybrid** (default): Minimum 3 days/week in the assigned office.
- **Full Remote**: Requires Director-level approval and is only available
  for roles explicitly designated "remote-eligible" by the role's job code.
- **Full-Time Office**: Required for roles that handle physical records,
  regulated healthcare data on-site, or lab/clinical work.

## Equipment
Company provides a laptop, monitor, and a one-time $300 home-office stipend
for approved full-remote employees. Hybrid employees are not eligible for
the home-office stipend.

## Cross-Border Remote Work
Employees may not work remotely from a country other than their country of
employment for more than 20 consecutive business days without prior approval
from HR and Legal, due to tax and labor law implications.

## Review Cadence
Manager and employee review the work arrangement every 6 months.

## Contact
Workplace Experience Team - workplace@company.com
